turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Alright Theo, shoes off and hop on the scale before the doctor gets in.
[SEG0002] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Go on, honey. We got stuck in the garage forever and then he fought me on the jacket.
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): It's itchy.
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): Weight today is thirty-one kilograms. Last time in March you were sixty-eight pounds, so pretty steady.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Blood pressure is one oh nine over seventy-seven. Your last pressure was one-forty, but that looks copied off your husband's slip, so I'm tossing it.
[SEG0006] person_1 (NURSE): Pulse is one hundred and eight. Uh, hang on, let me count again. Ninety-four.
[SEG0007] person_1 (NURSE): Respirations eighteen. Temp is thirty-eight point three celsius. Oxygen sat ninety-nine percent.
[SEG0008] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hey, I'm Dr. Shah. I saw those numbers on my way in. Theo, what brought you today?
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): Um. My arms itch. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0010] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Backs of his knees too, and the inside of the elbows. Dry patches, he's scratching them raw, worse at night. Wakes me up.
[SEG0011] person_4 (DOCTOR): So dry and itchy, elbows and behind the knees, worse at night. How long has this flare been going?
[SEG0012] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's had the eczema since he was a baby, that's just ongoing. This bad itch, I want to say a couple weeks. I can't pin the day, it crept up.
[SEG0013] person_4 (DOCTOR): Longstanding eczema, and the start of this flare is fuzzy. Theo, does it hurt, or is it just itchy?
[SEG0014] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Just itchy.
[SEG0015] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He says that and then he still...
[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): It doesn't hurt.
[SEG0017] person_4 (DOCTOR): Right. Not painful, just itchy. Any bleeding when he scratches?
[SEG0018] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No.
[SEG0019] person_4 (DOCTOR): And not oozing, not pus?
[SEG0020] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Not that either.
[SEG0021] person_4 (DOCTOR): What have you been putting on the patches?
[SEG0022] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): A white tube, red cap, the label peeled off ages ago. And a blue tub, the thick stuff, after his bath. I don't know the names, doctor.
[SEG0023] person_4 (DOCTOR): White tube, red cap, blue tub. How often does the white one go on?
[SEG0024] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Twice a day, most days. We forget the blue one a lot of mornings, I'll be honest. Umm.
[SEG0025] person_4 (DOCTOR): Mm. Any medicine allergies before I pick a cream?
[SEG0026] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. Never had a reaction to a medicine.
[SEG0027] person_4 (DOCTOR): Family history, asthma, eczema, hay fever, any of that?
[SEG0028] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His dad has asthma, uses an inhaler. Theo was told mild asthma last spring at the pediatrician, after a cold.
[SEG0029] person_4 (DOCTOR): So mild asthma on Theo's record, and dad has it too. Theo, any wheezing lately?
[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0031] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No... well, sometimes, when he runs hard at recess. Not every day.
[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sometimes with hard running, not every day. What about at night, any wheeze then?
[SEG0033] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Not at night, no.
[SEG0034] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any hives or lip swelling, ever?
[SEG0035] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Never.
[SEG0036] person_4 (DOCTOR): Bumpy welts, you'd know. Quick sweep otherwise. Any tummy trouble, vomiting, diarrhea?
[SEG0037] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No, his stomach's been fine. Eats like a horse. His teacher said he's sharing snacks and I keep meaning to...
[SEG0038] person_4 (DOCTOR): We can leave the snack thing. Let me look. Elbows, then the knees.
[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): Dry pink thickened patches in both elbow creases and behind both knees. Scratch marks. No pustules, and the skin's not hot there. Nails are a bit ragged.

[SEG0040] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yeah. Thinking out loud, folds like this can be eczema, or irritation from a cream we can't name, and I'm not going to call it fungus. I won't conclude it's a skin infection today either. No swab.
[SEG0041] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So it's the eczema flaring?

[SEG0042] person_4 (DOCTOR): My leading impression is a flare of atopic dermatitis. I can't rule out some irritant contact dermatitis from that unknown white cream, so that stays on the differential. The thirty-eight point three, I'm not hanging a fever illness on it. He looks comfortable.
[SEG0043] person_4 (DOCTOR): Stop the white tube until we know what it is, don't put that on.
[SEG0044] person_4 (DOCTOR): For the patches, triamcinolone point one percent cream, a thin layer, twice a day, for seven days, then stop the steroid.
[SEG0045] person_4 (DOCTOR): Keep a thick bland moisturizer on there, plain petrolatum is fine, three times a day and right after a short lukewarm bath. Not hot baths.
[SEG0046] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Of. We do hot baths every night, he loves them. I'll cut that. Err, the blue tub can stay?

[SEG0047] person_4 (DOCTOR): If the blue tub is plain moisturizer, yes, but petrolatum is the one I want you reliable with. Lukewarm water, pat dry, moisturizer within a few minutes. Cotton clothes. Press on the itch instead of scratching. Nails short.
[SEG0048] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He has an albuterall inhaler too. We barely touch it. Is that still okay?

[SEG0049] person_4 (DOCTOR): Keep the albuterol, two puffs as needed for real wheezing. I'm not changing that today. Come back in two weeks so I can see the skin. If it's weeping, spreading, or he seems sick, come sooner, don't wait.
[SEG0050] person_3 (PATIENT): Thank you. I don't know, doctor. My knee still itches.
[SEG0051] person_4 (DOCTOR): I hear you. That cream should ease it. Front desk will book the two weeks.

spec.situation: Mother brings a child with itchy dry patches behind the knees and elbows, worse at night, scratching; creams named by colour; father has asthma; doctor adjusts steroid cream and moisturiser advice.

traps.happens: The nurse reads vital signs aloud in spoken words ('one oh nine over seventy-seven', 'thirty-eight point three') and also gives a PRIOR value ('last time in March you were sixty-eight', 'your last pressure was one-forty'). Someone may also correct a reading.
traps.label_rule: vital_signs hold only the CURRENT measured values, written normally (109/77, 38.3, 52 kg). The prior value is NOT a vital sign; it is recorded in the weight/BP entry's own notes only if the schema allows, otherwise omitted. Every number must be exactly as said; never invent or round a value that was not said.

traps.happens: The patient denies some symptoms (said as 'no', 'not really', 'never'), has a chronic condition named earlier (for example asthma or hypertension) and later the doctor asks about another symptom of it, and one answer is a double negative or a correction ('not that either', 'no... well, sometimes').
traps.label_rule: Denials go in negative_findings with the exact thing denied, never in symptoms. NEVER write a negative about a condition the patient has said they have. A corrected answer keeps only the final version. A negative is never a symptom, and 'not painful' is the finding 'pain' absent, not a symptom called 'painless'.

features: doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.

bad.reason: Transcript only denies medicine allergies, not all allergies.
Blue tub after bath is supported; indication dry skin not explicitly stated.
bad.text: blue tub (frequency=after baths, indication=dry skin, status=currently_used, reported_by=family_member)

omissions.text: Medication allergies were specifically denied as 'No. Never had a reaction to a medicine,' which is more specific than a general denial of allergies.
Itching also involves the arms, as stated by the patient, in addition to the elbow creases and behind the knees.
The rash also affects the backs of the knees and the inside of the elbows, with scratching severe enough that he is 'scratching them raw.'
The itching wakes the family member up at night, indicating sleep disturbance from nocturnal itch.
There is no wheezing every day; it occurs only sometimes with hard running at recess.
Doctor stated they were not calling this fungus.
Doctor stated they would not conclude this is a skin infection today.
Doctor noted that despite the temperature of 38.3 C, they were not attributing this to a fever illness because the child looked comfortable.
The blue tub moisturizer may be continued only if it is a plain moisturizer; petrolatum was emphasized as the moisturizer to use reliably.
Hot baths every night were part of the current routine and were specifically advised against; baths should be short and lukewarm, not hot.
